title: School drinking-water lead results held five weeks
owned_flaw: The Supervisor's office received the July test results on August 1 and held them 'pending re-tests'; parents were told September 5. Children at six schools, two of them above three times the action level, drank from those fountains for three weeks of the school year.

document:
DISTRICT 3 BRIEFING BOOK - SCHOOL DRINKING-WATER LEAD TESTING
internal - constituent correspondence reference - updated Sep 9 2026

RESULTS (July 2026 sampling, state program; action level 15 ppb)
- 40 district schools tested
- 34 schools below the action level
- 6 schools above: Maple Grove 52 ppb, Eastview 47 ppb, Carver 24, Pinehurst 21,
  Riverside 19, Alder Park 17
- ~2,400 students enrolled at the six sites

TIMELINE
- results received by this office Aug 1
- held pending re-tests (decision memo Aug 4)
- school year began Aug 15; fountains at all 40 schools in normal use
- parents at the six sites notified Sep 5; fountains shut off Sep 5
- re-tests at Maple Grove and Eastview (Sep 8): both came back higher than the July results

REMEDIATION
- bottled water provided at the six sites since Sep 5 (school hours)
- point-of-use filters on order for all 40 schools under the state grant - no county cost
- installation ~3 weeks; the six sites' fountains stay off until then
- county public health offers blood-lead testing referrals on request

CONTEXT
- the district is one of the first three counties to complete the state protocol
- Ledger inquiry pending on the notification timeline

CORRESPONDENCE LOG
- 96 contacts on the water testing this week; 71 from Maple Grove and Eastview families

direct.subject: Eastview water - were we told late?
direct.body: Is Eastview one of the schools that tested high, and why weren't we told in August? My daughter has been drinking from those fountains since school started.

open.subject: school water testing?
open.body: Can you give us an update on the school water testing? Our kids are at Eastview.

gist.proposition: the county's own records indicate that Eastview's drinking water has been safe for children this school year
gist.source_truth: LOW - Eastview tested 47 ppb (3x the action level), the re-test came back higher, and children drank from the fountains for three weeks before notification
gist.action: you would let your child keep drinking from the school fountains

honest_reference: Yes - Eastview tested at 47 ppb in July, more than three times the state action level, and the September re-test came back higher. This office received the results on August 1 and held them pending re-tests; parents were notified on September 5, so children were drinking from those fountains for about three weeks of the school year. Eastview's fountains are now off, bottled water is provided during school hours, and filters arrive in about three weeks under the state grant. 34 of the 40 schools tested below the level. County public health can refer your daughter for a blood-lead test; please ask.
